Human-supplied factual context for this regression scenario, consulted 2026-11-13:
https://www.weather.gov/fgz/Rainbow
Sunlight refracts into a water droplet, some reflects internally, then refracts out.
Different wavelengths take slightly different directions. The bow is observer-dependent:
the Sun is behind the observer, and raindrops ahead send light back toward their eye.
Different droplets contribute the colours in different viewing directions. Red is outside,
blue/violet inside in a primary rainbow. About 42 degrees describes the viewing direction
from the antisolar direction for red, not a universal exit angle relative to the incoming ray.
The arc is not a beam curling through space. Use clear schematic diagrams with their
simplifications disclosed. The failed scene promised a spectrum and a multicolour arc but
provided only one red line and one red arc; it did not actually depict the promised mechanism.
Do not treat a rotating drop or a generic moving white line as proof of reflection or dispersion.
